about:
# Ultimate Profession Master

Formerly TOG Profession Master.

Stop whispering every alchemist in your guild to ask "is your transmute up?" and stop logging into five different alts to remember who knows the recipe you need. Ultimate Profession Master keeps a live, shared view of every guildmate's professions, recipes, and cooldowns — and lets you mail reagents straight to the crafter without typing a single character name.

Works on Classic Era / Anniversary, TBC Classic, Wrath Classic, Cataclysm Classic, and Mists of Pandaria Classic, with early support for WoW Forever and Retail.

## Works even better with

- **Ultimate Bank** — see your guild bank's stock next to every reagent, and request it from a banker in two clicks. [Details](#ultimate-bank-integration)
- **Ultimate Questbook** — one click on a recipe you're missing guides you to the best vendor or drop for its scroll. [Details](#ultimate-questbook-integration)
- **Personal Shopper** — a **[List]** button on the Missing Recipes tab adds the recipe scroll to your Personal Shopper shopping list.

All are optional: install any of them and its buttons appear automatically.

## Quickstart

1. Install via [CurseForge](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/togprofessionmaster) (recommended — handles dependencies automatically) or drop the folder into `Interface\AddOns`
2. `/reload` or restart WoW
3. Click the **UPM minimap button** to open the main window
4. Open your own profession windows (Alchemy, Tailoring, etc.) at least once on each character — UPM scans them automatically and starts syncing with the guild

That's it. Within a minute or two you'll see your guildmates' recipes and cooldowns alongside your own.

## What it does

**Profession Browser** — Every recipe known by anyone in your guild, with a list of crafters per recipe. On WoW Forever this includes the Herbalism, Skinning and Fishing camp objects. Filter by profession, search by name, see who's online, right-click to whisper the crafter.

**Cooldowns Tab** — Every guildmate's active and ready profession cooldowns in one view: transmutes, Mooncloth, Salt Shaker, Northrend Research, Icy Prism, Truegold, Living Steel, JC daily cuts, and more. Hit the one-click **[Mail]** button to send the crafter a pre-composed supply mail with every reagent of that cooldown on it — one mail per cooldown, even for a two-reagent transmute like Arcanite; the click splits whatever stacks need splitting, attaches them all and fills in the recipient, and it sends nothing at all if you are short of any reagent. A crafter on another realm gets the mail on their own realm, and if the game refuses the mail, chat says why. Click **[Mail]** again once the mail is ready and it sends. A **Sent** column then shows how long ago you supplied that crafter ("5m ago", "3h ago", date and time on hover), and clears itself once they use the cooldown. The reagent column is white when your bags hold enough of it to fill that mail and grey when they don't, so a glance down the list tells you which cooldowns you can actually feed — and it recolours as you loot or send things, without a tab switch.

**Missing Recipes Tab** — Pick a character and a profession and see every recipe scroll they haven't learned yet, with where to obtain it (vendor, drop, quest, container, fishing). Filter to a single profession or search by name. **Vendor only** narrows the list to scrolls you can buy from a vendor your faction can use, and a scroll that needs reputation shows once your standing is high enough. The **On AH** column shows each scroll's cheapest buyout at your last ItemDB Auction House scan, and it stays after you close the Auction House. A **Guild** view shows recipes *nobody* in the guild knows, which is the coverage gap worth acting on. Rank-up books (Expert, Artisan and so on) drop off the list once you have outgrown them. A **[Where]** button opens every vendor, drop and zone for the recipe's scroll, with drop chances and map coordinates (from ItemDB). With **Ultimate Questbook** installed, a **[Guide]** button routes you to the scroll ([details](#ultimate-questbook-integration)). With **Personal Shopper** installed, a **[List]** button adds the scroll to your shopping list. **Can learn now** hides recipes the character isn't skilled enough for yet. **Share List** copies every character's missing scrolls as text to paste on your other account; their characters then appear in the Character list marked "(shared)", and **All characters** lists every scroll any of them needs, once each with who wants it, for one trip to the Auction House. Importing a character again replaces their earlier list, and **Forget** removes one. On TBC there is an optional filter to hide recipes from content phases that are not live yet — it ships off, so by default nothing is hidden from you.

**Guild Tab** — Who in the guild has which profession, at what skill, and with which specialization. Specializations are inferred from the spec-gated recipes a crafter knows, so they show up even for people who never announced them. Gathering professions are included, and a profession with nobody in it is shown at zero — coverage gaps are the thing you actually want to see. Search by profession, specialization or character name, and set **Min skill** / **Max skill** to find, say, a 250–260 tailor.

**Crafting Tab** — A full crafting screen in UPM's own style, including a drag-to-reorder craft queue (Craft All crafts one recipe's full batch per click, because the game needs a click for each recipe) and a cost-to-craft with profit preview (a reagent a vendor sells is costed at the vendor price, never an auction listing). Optionally takes over the default profession window (`/upm craft`). Enchanting is supported, recipe tooltips included. A hunter's Beast Training shares Enchanting's window on Classic and TBC; the takeover leaves it to the game, so pets can always be trained.

**Profit Planner** — What's worth making right now, using auction prices from **ItemDB**: its own Auction House scan, or Auctionator, Auctioneer and TradeSkillMaster if you run them. Which sources are used, and in what order, is set once in ItemDB (`/itemdb`, or the **Price sources** button in UPM's settings) and applies to every TOG addon; the Historical view uses only the sources that keep a history. No other pricing addon required.

**Allied Guilds (cross-guild sharing)** — Share professions and cooldowns between two guilds. Set up under **Settings → Cross-Guild** by an officer or the guild leader; it is bilateral by design, so both sides opt in, and it shares the whole guild's data rather than just yours. The allied-guild list and the allied rosters live in **GuildRoster** (also editable with `/guildroster sisters`), so every addon in the family on your account — this one, Ultimate Tools, Ultimate Bank — reads one list and one set of rosters rather than each keeping its own. Pull an allied roster once from any online member of that guild (`/upm pullroster <Name>`) and GuildRoster keeps it current from then on, for the whole guild. Allied guild members carry a short tag after their name (`Ahmbrai <Other>`) in every list, picked automatically so two guilds never share one; set your own under **Settings → Cross-Guild → Allied guild tags**. The tags come from GuildRoster too (1.4.0 or newer), so every TOG addon uses the same ones.

**Shopping List + Reagent Tracker** — Queue any recipe to your shopping list. The floating Reagent Tracker shows a live total of everything you need vs. what's in your bags; like Questie's tracker it stays up through Escape, `/reload` and logout, and its **-** / **+** button folds it to its title bar. It has its own scale and opacity sliders under **Settings → Display**, and a dark background whose opacity the slider sets (the text never fades). You get a chat alert once your bags hold every reagent for a craft on your list. **Share List** on the Recipes toolbar exports the list as text and imports one pasted from another account or a friend: it adds to your list without replacing anything, and each item shows which other character wants it.

**[AH] buttons** — Open the auction house and press ItemDB's scan button in its top-left corner: one pass scans the whole house. Afterwards, every row in UPM whose item is listed (shopping-list reagents, cooldown reagents, missing recipes, crafting reagents) gets an **[AH]** button you can click to jump straight to the AH browse search.

### Ultimate Bank integration

When **Ultimate Bank** is installed, every reagent shows a **[Bank]** button when the guild bank has stock — in the Professions tab's recipe details, the Cooldowns tab, Missing Recipes, the Crafting tab, the shopping list and the Reagent Tracker. One click opens a request dialog: pick the banker, set the quantity, send. The maximum is the one Ultimate Bank enforces: the officer's request percentage of that banker's stock, less what you already have on order from them. View-only bankers aren't offered, and when an order is refused you see Ultimate Bank's own reason. While Ultimate Bank's shop is open, the order goes in as a shop purchase with its price estimate shown in the dialog; the bank character sets the final price when it's filled. The button carries Ultimate Bank's own status dot — green when your copy of that bank is current, red or yellow when a newer copy is on its way, grey when the only newer copy can't reach your client — so you can tell at a glance whether the stock behind it is current; hover for each banker's count and status.

### Ultimate Questbook integration

When **Ultimate Questbook** is installed, the Missing Recipes tab can take you to the recipe you're missing. A **[Guide]** button on every missing recipe starts a route to the best place for its scroll in one click — one in your current zone first, then a vendor, then the best drop chance. Clicking any vendor, drop or zone in the **[Where]** window guides you there instead. The guide stops by itself once the scroll is in your bags, and Ultimate Questbook's own stop button sits in the main window's bottom row, beside the gear, on every tab, to cancel the route.

### More features

**Cooldown ready alerts** — Switch on an alert for any cooldown on the Cooldowns tab and you are told when it comes up. A setting mutes them in raids, dungeons and battlegrounds; any you missed fire the moment you leave.

**Crafter Online Alerts** — Chat ping when a guildmate who can craft something on your shopping list comes online.

**Item Tooltips** — Hover any item in your bags, the AH, a vendor, or a chat link, and you'll see which guildmates know how to craft it, with their skill rank and online status.

**Recipe details on every tooltip** — Hover a recipe scroll, or the item it makes, anywhere in the game: skill-up difficulty in the game's own tier colours, where the recipe comes from (trainer, drop, vendor, quest, container; on WoW Forever, the Merchant's Favor vendor by name with the recipe's price), and a red **Unlearned** list of which of *your* characters could still learn it, with their skill rank and specialisation. The source data is keyed by the recipe rather than by a scroll item, so it answers for the roughly one recipe in three that is trainer-taught and has no scroll at all — 74.9% of Vanilla recipes, against 44.6% for an item-keyed lookup. **This renders even if you run RecipeMaster**, and that is deliberate as of v1.0.7. UPM's block is not a duplicate of RM's: only UPM tells you which of *your own* characters could still learn the recipe, and which guildmates can craft it. Standing down to avoid overlapping two rows also withheld the rows nothing else in the game provides. A setting reverts to the old behaviour (RM owns the game's tooltips, UPM fills in the ones RM can't see) or switches the block off entirely.

**Choose what each tooltip shows** — Settings > Item tooltip has an on/off switch for every line UPM adds: crafters, recipe difficulty, recipe sources, your unlearned characters, vendor buy price, vendor sell price and the item/recipe IDs. The vendor sell row also stands down on its own when the game is already showing a sell price.

**Item links behave like the rest of the game** — Shift-click any item name, reagent or recipe anywhere in the addon to link it in chat; ctrl-click to preview it in the dressing room. Hold the compare modifier over an item to see it side by side with what you're wearing. All of it goes through Blizzard's own handler, so it honours whatever you have those modifiers bound to rather than assuming shift and ctrl. If you'd rather have the full stock tooltip everywhere instead of UPM's trimmed one, there's a setting for that (off by default).

**Vendor buy *and* sell price, on every item** — Hover anything, anywhere: your bags, the auction house, a vendor, a chat link. Not just recipes. Two rows, and each one appears only when its number is real, so you never get a confident zero.

**Sell** is what a vendor pays you, the same figure TradeSkillMaster labels "Vendor Sell Price". **Buy** is what a vendor charges, which is a different number entirely — the two differ by roughly 4x, and cost-to-craft totals elsewhere in the addon deliberately use the buy price, because that is what a reagent actually costs you.

Buy comes from ItemDB's three-tier lookup: Auctionator's vendor cache, then prices captured live from vendors *you* have opened, then ItemDB's base price. Where you have met the vendor yourself the figure reflects your reputation discount rather than a book value. Sell asks the client first and falls back to ItemDB, so unlike most vendor-price lines it still answers for an item your client has never cached.

Nobody else shows both: TSM and Leatrix Plus show sell only, AllTheThings shows neither, and the game itself shows neither in your bags.

### How UPM behaves on a tooltip that isn't its own

Hovering an item can involve several addons writing into one shared frame. UPM follows four rules so it never degrades what the rest of your UI puts there.

**Nothing drawn on a UPM tooltip can stretch it, including other addons' lines.** A WoW tooltip has a preset wrap width the engine derives from your resolution, UI scale and font, and a line opts into it with a flag that defaults to *off*. One line that doesn't opt in ignores the preset and widens the whole frame — everyone's content with it. UPM passes that flag on every line it writes, and forces it on for the duration of any third-party render, so an addon that never heard of the flag still gets held to the game's width. Exactly one line is left unwrapped: the recipe title, because something has to claim a natural width or the frame collapses to the bare preset and an item name that the game fits on one line breaks onto two. No width is measured, and none is hardcoded — a hardcoded one would be right on the machine it was measured on and wrong on yours.

**UPM's block renders after the integrations it draws itself.** On tooltips UPM builds — the recipe browser, Missing Recipes — other addons' contributions are drawn first and ours last, matching the order a stock tooltip uses. It also means a fault in UPM's block can't take anything else down with it: before v1.0.7 an error partway through our block silently deleted AllTheThings, TradeSkillMaster and RecipeMaster from the tooltip, because the raise aborted before their content was rendered.

On the game's own tooltips — your bags, the auction house, a chat link — UPM appends wherever the hook chain puts it, which is not necessarily last. Addon tooltip order there is decided by load order and hook registration across every addon you run, and no single addon controls it.

**UPM hands the tooltip back exactly as it found it.** The tooltip you hover is a single frame shared by the whole UI, and the game never resets a width once something has widened it — that has to be undone deliberately by whoever set it. Through v1.0.6 one hover of UPM's help icon widened *every tooltip in the game*, ours and every other addon's, for the rest of the session. That's fixed, and if another addon has legitimately set its own minimum width, UPM restores that value rather than clearing it.

**Every tab uses the game's own tooltip, including Missing Recipes.** That tab used a private tooltip frame from v0.7.5 to v1.0.6, to sidestep a third-party addon raising on recipe scrolls it hadn't cached. The cost was that its rows looked different from the rest of the game and no other addon's tooltip additions appeared on them. That addon has been rewritten since, so the private frame is gone and Missing Recipes behaves like everything else.

## Slash Commands

Every command also works as `/togpm`, the old name.

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `/upm` | Open the main window |
| `/upm reagents` | Open the floating Reagent Tracker |
| `/upm minimap` | Show the minimap button (if you've hidden it) |
| `/upm settings` | Open the settings panel |
| `/upm craft` | Toggle the crafting-window takeover on or off |
| `/upm sync` | Force a fresh sync with the guild now |
| `/upm status` | Show sync status and online member count |
| `/upm versioncheck` | Check which guildmates are running which version |
| `/upm purge` | Open the purge-data dialog (clear stored guild data) |
| `/upm help` | Show all commands, including the diagnostics below |

If sync isn't working, these are the ones worth running before opening a bug report — paste the output into the Discord:

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `/upm commtest` | Asks whether your server actually relays guild addon messages at all. Some private cores don't, and nothing else can work if that's the answer |
| `/upm dsstatus` | Sync engine status: what's been sent, received, and refused |
| `/upm xgdiag` | Cross-guild diagnostics — why an allied guild's data isn't arriving |
| `/upm whyvisible <Name>` | Explains why a particular character is (or isn't) shown |
| `/upm perf` | How long each window open, tab draw, background build and incoming sync took this session; the game's own record of every addon's worst frame since login (so a pause is attributed to whichever addon owned it); and how large each part of your saved data is. If the game pauses, run this straight afterwards and paste it |
| `/acq status` | The comm queue's own view: which sends are in flight, stalled, or refused |

## Requirements

Installing from CurseForge pulls these in automatically. Installing by hand means fetching them yourself, and the addon will not load without them:

**Ace3**, **DeltaSync**, **AceCommQueue-1.0**, **VersionCheck-1.0**, **GuildRoster**, **ProfessionDB**, **ItemDB**, **LibAceGUIWidgets**, **LibDBIcon-1.0**.

LibDBIcon-1.0 is bundled on WoW Forever, where it is not published yet; everywhere else it is a separate addon.

Keep **AceCommQueue-1.0** current in particular — it is the layer that queues addon traffic, and older copies mistook ordinary server throttling for a fault and reported it as an error. **GuildRoster 0.7.0 or newer** is needed for cross-guild sharing: it holds the allied-guild list and rosters for every TOG addon; on an older copy the addon runs normally with cross-guild sharing off. **ItemDB carrying LibItemDB 25 or newer** is needed for any auction price: since v1.1.0 the Auction House scanner, the Auctionator / Auctioneer / TSM connections and the price-source settings all live there; on an older ItemDB you get vendor prices only, and no [AH] buttons.

## Settings

All settings live in WoW's standard Options panel: **ESC → Options → AddOns → Ultimate Profession Master**. Or click the gear icon on the main window, or type `/upm settings`.

Settings include cooldown-ready alarms, crafter-online alerts, instance-mute toggle, periodic reminder cadence, window scale and background opacity (turn the window see-through without fading its text), the same pair for the Reagent Tracker (its opacity runs down to 0%, no background at all), and more — every option has a hover tooltip explaining what it does. Price sources (which of Auctionator / Auctioneer / TSM / the ItemDB scan are used, and in what order) are set in ItemDB's own window; the **Price sources (ItemDB)...** button here opens it, and the choices you had made in UPM before v1.1.0 were carried over on your first login.

## Need Help?

Bug reports, feature requests, questions, or just chatting: **[Join the Discord](https://discord.com/invite/bY2R5TmBSz)**.

## Credits

**Pimptasty** — author and maintainer.

Built on the [Ace3](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/ace3) library suite (AceAddon, AceGUI, AceDB, AceConfig, AceComm, AceSerializer, AceTimer, AceConsole), plus [DeltaSync](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/deltasync) for the peer-to-peer sync engine, [GuildRoster](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/libguildroster) for guild membership and online state, [ItemDB](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/libitemdb) for item stats, vendor prices and recipe-scroll data, [AceCommQueue](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/acecommqueue), [VersionCheck](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/versioncheck), LibAceGUIWidgets for the shared window and list widgets, LibDataBroker, and LibDBIcon.

Optional integrations: [Ultimate Bank](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/togbankclassic) for guild-bank reagent buttons ([details](#ultimate-bank-integration)); Ultimate Questbook for guiding you to where a missing recipe's scroll is sold or drops ([details](#ultimate-questbook-integration)).

### Data sources

Recipe data comes from [ProfessionDB](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/libprofessiondb),
built from Blizzard's own client data via [wago.tools](https://wago.tools/). This
addon ships no recipe data of its own and generates none — ProfessionDB owns the
whole pipeline, so every table is correct for the exact client version you are
running rather than being an all-expansion merge.

Two things the client does not know are derived from community projects at build
time, and shipped as static tables:

- **Where a recipe comes from** — trainer, vendor, quest, container and drop
  sources are derived from the [TrinityCore](https://github.com/TrinityCore) and
  [AzerothCore](https://github.com/azerothcore) world databases, which
  reverse-engineered and tested them. The client stores none of it. They ship in
  ProfessionDB, with the npc names alongside the ids, and the npc names are
  English only because the world databases are not localized.
- **Which TBC content phase gates a recipe** — the `phase` tags behind the
  optional Missing Recipes phase filter are derived from
  [AllTheThings](https://github.com/ATTWoWAddon/AllTheThings) (MIT), via its raid,
  reputation and patch metadata. That filter **ships off** as of v1.0.8: by
  default you see every recipe, and you turn it on if you would rather hide
  content that is not live on your realm yet. It defaulted to *on* before that,
  pinned to a phase number that had to be bumped by a release each time Blizzard
  opened one — which stopped happening, and quietly hid 194 real TBC recipes.

In every case the projects' files are **not** redistributed: only the factual
mappings are extracted and re-expressed in this addon's own format, and each
project is gratefully acknowledged.

# Ultimate Profession Master Changelog (formerly TOG Profession Master)

## [v1.11.3] (2026-11-21) - WoW Forever: a blocked Crafting tab says what to do

### Bug Fixes

- **A blocked profession open on WoW Forever left the Crafting tab blank.**
  The client still sometimes refuses `C_TradeSkillUI.OpenTradeSkill` from the
  tab click (`ADDON_ACTION_BLOCKED` "UNKNOWN()", operator's BugSack and taint
  log 2026-11-21: the block is on the call itself, and it happens even on the
  first open after a login). My v1.11.2 note that a first click after a
  `/reload` is safe was wrong. The cause is still not known; another WoW
  Forever addon found the same call blocked from addon code
  (cjber/commissions-forever#194). The tab now says "The game blocked opening
  X this time. Pick it from the menu above, or open it from your spellbook."
  instead of the plain "Open X to view" prompt. `Engine:OpenProfession` returns
  `false, "blocked"` when the block watcher saw a block, and counts a blocked
  call as failed even when it returned `true` -- in game it did exactly that
  (`-> true BLOCKED(BLOCKED)`). Location: `Modules/Crafting/CraftingEngine.lua`,
  `GUI/CraftingTab.lua`, `Locale/enUS.lua` (`CraftOpenBlocked`).
- **One click raised the block error twice.** After the first call, the engine
  asked again when Blizzard's window had just been shown and the wrong
  profession came up; when the first call was blocked, that retry only added a
  second error. It no longer asks again after a block (one BugSack entry per
  click since, in game 2026-11-21). Location:
  `Modules/Crafting/CraftingEngine.lua`.

### Improvements

- **Specs** for the blocked open: no retry after a block, the `"blocked"`
  reason, a blocked call that returned `true`, and no reason when nothing
  opened without a block. Location: `Tests/craftsuppress_spec.lua`.
- **`Locale/enUS.lua`**: two locale lines that had been written on one line
  are split back onto their own lines.

---

## [v1.11.2] (2026-11-20) - WoW Forever: Crafting tab profession open

### Bug Fixes

- **Clicking the Crafting tab on WoW Forever still raised
  `ADDON_ACTION_BLOCKED` ("UNKNOWN()")** (operator's BugSack, 2026-11-13 to
  2026-11-19, 2x per click from both `OpenTradeSkill` calls). My v1.11.0 fix
  blamed combat and added an `InCombatLockdown()` gate; that was the wrong
  cause -- these blocks came from ordinary tab clicks with the gate already in
  place. Blizzard's own caller loads the profession window
  (`ProfessionsFrame_LoadUI`) BEFORE `OpenTradeSkill`
  (`Blizzard_FrameXMLUtil/ProfessionsUtil.lua:84`, forever tree) and ours did
  not, so a first open loaded Blizzard_Professions inside the call. The engine
  now loads it first, in Blizzard's order. This is Peer Review's H4 from
  2026-09-29; the operator's first tab click after a `/reload` raised no
  error with it in place (in game, 2026-11-20). The block watcher also dropped
  every block not named `OpenTradeSkill`/`CastSpell`, so this one never reached
  `/upm opendebug`; while an open is in flight it now records a block under any
  name. Specs in `Tests/craftsuppress_spec.lua`. Location:
  `Modules/Crafting/CraftingEngine.lua`.

---

## [v1.11.1] (2026-11-18) - WoW Forever's new recipes on the Professions tab, shift-click links in the Crafting tab, a full-size minimap icon

### Bug Fixes

- **WoW Forever's own recipes were missing from the Professions and Missing
  Recipes tabs.** Reported in game: Brawler's Leather Gloves showed in the
  Crafting tab but not on the Professions tab. WoW Forever reports Interface
  16001, so `addon.isVanilla` is true there, and the recipe gate treated it as
  Classic Era -- whose "Season of Discovery" rule hides every recipe id at or
  above 200000. Every recipe Forever added (Brawler's is 1255130) has an id far
  above that, so all of them were dropped, along with the other Era-only
  heuristics about the 1.15 client's shared spell tables. The gate now excludes
  WoW Forever from "Era" (`addon.IsForeverClient`, ProfessionDB's own
  detection, now public); Forever's data is built from its own client tables,
  so those heuristics never applied to it. Specs: the "WoW Forever" block in
  `Tests/recipegate_spec.lua`. Location: `Modules/RecipeGate.lua`,
  `TOGProfessionMaster.lua`.
- **Shift-click did nothing on the Crafting tab's reagents or recipe name.**
  The detail panel's reagent list had a hover tooltip but no click handler,
  and the recipe name had none either. Both now go through
  `addon.ItemLink.Click`, the same as the Browser tab: a modified left click
  links the item in chat (or opens the dressing room, depending on your key
  bindings). Specs in `Tests/craftingtab_controls_spec.lua`. Location:
  `GUI/CraftingTab.lua`.
- **The minimap icon was cut flat, then tiny, in Ultimate Tools' square
  button bag.** The crop had been tuned by eye for the round minimap slot,
  where LibDBIcon's ring hides the rim, and cut about 1 px off the right of
  the coin and 2 px off the bottom. Then the bag stopped honouring addon
  crops and draws each icon file whole (TOGTools `BagIconCoord`), and the UPM
  art had its coin in only 44x46 px of the 64x64 file where UGR's and UTr's
  fill 56x58 -- so UPM drew noticeably smaller than its siblings. The art
  (`icons/UPM_MMB_Icon.tga`) is rescaled so the coin fills the same box as
  theirs (x 4..59, y 2..58), and `iconCoords` is re-measured to the 58 px
  square on it for the round minimap. Specs in `Tests/minimap_spec.lua` read
  the TGA and check the crop against it; `Tests/tga_bounds.lua` prints the
  coin box of UPM's art beside its siblings'. Location: `GUI/MinimapButton.lua`,
  `icons/UPM_MMB_Icon.tga`.

---

# Ultimate Profession Master Changelog (formerly TOG Profession Master)

## [v1.10.3] (2026-11-12) - WoW Forever: guild sync works, no combat error, no trainer spam

### Bug Fixes

- **WoW Forever: no guildmate's professions ever showed, on any client**
  (Discord 2026-11-08, with a status screenshot reading sends=24 rcvs=176, so
  data was flowing). Forever names are regionally unique "First Last" with no
  realm, and `UnitName`'s second return there is the SURNAME. The character
  key was `UnitName("player") .. "-" .. realm`, i.e. "First-Realm", while
  LibGuildRoster keys Forever members "First Last" and its `NormalizeName`
  cuts an incoming "First-Realm" down to "First". Every guildmate's data was
  filed under a key no roster entry matched and the roster gate hid it; the
  own-echo check never matched either. `GetCharacterKey()` now returns
  `LibGuildRoster:GetNormalizedPlayer()` when the library's `RegionalNames()`
  is on, so the key matches the roster and the wire; every other client keeps
  "Name-Realm". At login on Forever the old "First-Realm" own key leaves the
  account-character set and goes to the roster-gated pending purge, so it
  does not linger as a phantom alt. A Forever player re-records their recipes
  by opening each profession window once. Location: `TOGProfessionMaster.lua`
  (GetCharacterKey, OnPlayerEnteringWorld). Spec: new
  `Tests/forevernames_spec.lua`.
- **WoW Forever: a search or filter in the Professions window stripped
  recipes from your character.** Forever has no `GetAllRecipeIDs`, only the
  window's filtered list, and the scan treats its list as the whole
  profession, so a filtered window removed the character from every recipe
  it did not show and shared that shortened set as authoritative. The scan
  now skips while any filter is active (the same reads as Blizzard's
  `Professions.IsUsingDefaultFilters`) and re-scans on the next list update.
  Location: `Compat.lua` (ModernRecipeListFiltered,
  GetModernLearnedRecipeIDs). Spec: `Tests/scanner_scan_spec.lua`.
- **WoW Forever / Retail: "attempt to compare local 'start' (a secret number
  value)" from the cooldown scan** (Discord 2026-11-07). `C_Spell.GetSpellCooldown`
  is `SecretWhenCooldownsRestricted`, so in combat its fields are secret.
  `addon.Spell.GetCooldown` now answers nil values plus a fifth `true` for a
  secret read; the scan skips that pass instead of mistaking "unreadable" for
  "ready", and the transmute diagnostic says to try again out of combat.
  Location: `Compat.lua`, `Scanner.lua` (ScanCooldowns),
  `TOGProfessionMaster.lua` (DumpTransmuteDiag). Specs:
  `Tests/compat_spec.lua`, `Tests/scanner_cooldowns_spec.lua`.
- **"Trainer scan: 0 new, 4 updated" printed after every spell learned at a
  class trainer** (Discord 2026-11-07). The trainer scan ran at any trainer
  and re-fired on each `TRAINER_UPDATE`. It now runs only where
  `IsTradeskillTrainer()` is true, and its summary is debug output only.
  Location: `Scanner.lua` (OnTrainerShow). Spec: new
  `Tests/scanner_trainer_spec.lua`.
- **`/togpm status` said every online guildmate had "(no data)" and 0 stored
  members, on every client.** It counted `gdb.guildData`, which nothing
  writes. It now reads the profession registry (`gdb.skills`). Location:
  `Scanner.lua` (PrintStatus).

### Improvements

- **Missing Recipes is ready for ItemDB's WoW Forever vendor locations.** No
  code change was needed: the where-to-get rows, the Vendor only filter and
  [Guide] read the same rows on Forever as on Classic; two comments that said
  Forever has no places were corrected. Location: `GUI/MissingRecipesTab.lua`.

## [v1.10.2] (2026-11-05) - Retail: no more error when a system message arrives

### Bug Fixes

- **Retail: "attempt to index local 'message' (a secret string value, while
  execution tainted by 'TOGProfessionMaster')"** (Discord 2026-11-05). Retail
  sometimes hands addons a `CHAT_MSG_SYSTEM` payload as a secret value;
  `type()` still answers "string", so the learned-recipe handler's guard let
  it through and `message:match` raised. `OnLearnMessage` now returns early
  when `issecretvalue(message)` is true, read through `_G` because the global
  exists only on the live client (FrameScriptDocumentation.lua), so every
  Classic flavour skips the check. The "No player named X is currently
  playing" chat filter read the same payload with `message:find` and gets the
  same guard, plus a `type()` check where it only tested for nil. A recipe
  learned while the message is secret is still recorded by the trade-skill
  scan the next time that profession window opens. Location: `Scanner.lua`
  (OnLearnMessage, InstallChatFilter). Specs: `Tests/scanner_learn_spec.lua`,
  new `Tests/scanner_chatfilter_spec.lua` (the filter had no spec before).

### Improvements

- **README rebranded and reorganised** -- a "Works even better with" section
  near the top, Ultimate Bank and Ultimate Questbook integrations as their own
  sections, and the cooldown ready alerts and Missing Recipes' Can learn now
  filter, both shipped features, now described. Location: `README.md`.
- **Dev replication script reaches the new WoW Forever install** --
  `_forever_` added to the target list, and a target is picked when its
  version folder exists rather than its `Interface\AddOns`, so a fresh install
  without an AddOns folder is no longer skipped silently; `-DryRun` no longer
  creates folders. Dev-only, not shipped. Location:
  `wow-version-replication.ps1`.
